edges.description: Colonizing S. aureus enters shaved beard follicles to establish folliculitis.
edges.source: Staphylococcus aureus Skin and Mucosal Colonization

edges.description: Untreated superficial folliculitis can extend deeper around the infected follicle.
Suppurative inflammation appears as fine pustules at beard follicle openings.
Deeper suppuration around an infected follicle forms a perifollicular nodule, the furuncle.
When several furuncles form and coalesce, the suppuration becomes a deep, communicating carbuncle.
Multiple furuncles that coalesce form a carbuncle.

The source reports beard-area staphylococcal folliculitis as often associated with shaving, which describes a predisposing setting for follicular infection rather than its cause; S. aureus is the cause.
